For eighty five years, St Francis School has offered children something increasingly rare, a proper childhood. Founded in Pewsey in 1941 with just four pupils, the school now sits in seventeen acres of the beautiful Pewsey Vale, where children climb, dig, sing, question and explore, where mud on knees is a sign of a morning well spent, and where every child is known by name.

Head’s Welcome
Welcome to St. Francis School
For eighty five years, St Francis School has offered children something increasingly rare, a proper childhood. Founded in Pewsey in 1941 with just four pupils, the school now sits in seventeen acres of the beautiful Pewsey Vale, where children climb, dig, sing, question and explore, where mud on knees is a sign of a morning well spent, and where every child is known by name.
I come to the headship of St Francis having previously led a school, and after a career spent working with children and families from all walks of life. That experience has taught me a simple truth, children flourish when the adults around them take both their learning and their happiness seriously. As the first female Head at St Francis in well over a decade, I bring everything I have learned over three decades in education as we take the school into its next era, honouring all that makes this school special while looking confidently to the future.
‘A happy childhood is perhaps the most fortunate gift in life’
It would be a mistake to think that a childhood-centred school is a soft one. Our academic standards are rigorous and our expectations are high. Children here are taught by specialist teachers in small classes, never in merged year groups, and they leave us as confident, articulate learners ready for the very best senior schools. We believe rigour and joy belong together, and that children work hardest for teachers who know them well.
The best way to understand St Francis School is to visit. Come and hear the noise of a wellies-and-waterproofs playtime on the field, watch our teams in action on the sports pitch, and join our forest school children building dens and lighting fires among the trees. See our classrooms at work and meet the children who make this place what it is. I would be delighted to show you around.
Karen Austin Headmistress

To contact the Head directly, please email head@stfpewsey.co.uk

Our school is part of the Inspired Learning Group (‘ILG’) of independent schools and nurseries. www.inspiredlearninggroup.co.uk.
ILG strives to create safe and inspiring educational environments where children can grow into positive and impactful members of society who will, one day in turn, shape the outlook of the next generation. Our schools and nurseries combine traditional values and forward-thinking ideas to help every single pupil realise their potential, so they are prepared to take on jobs that have not yet been invented.
ILG believes, first and foremost, in putting your child at the heart of everything we do. We endeavour to provide educational excellence within a culture of care to nurture each pupil the best we can. We want to offer a wide range of opportunities, both academic and extra-curricular, so that all our children are endowed with the spirit to aspire and become twenty first century citizens.
The main functions of Governance across the ILG schools and nurseries are to:
Ensure compliance with legal and DfE requirements
Raise standards through monitoring and evaluating performance

More Than a Holiday. A Summer to Remember.
St Francis School Summer Day Camp 2026 | Pewsey, Wiltshire | 20th July – 21st August Six weeks of sport, creativity, team challenges and growing confidence — set in the beautiful grounds of St Francis School, Pewsey. Open to all children, Reception to Year 8. You do not need to be a St Francis pupil to join us.

A Summer Built Around Your Child
We know that childhood is a special and precious time. At St Francis, that belief shapes everything we do — and our Summer Day Camp in Wiltshire is no different.
Each week of camp is thoughtfully crafted to nurture each child’s individual confidence, creativity and sense of belonging. From the first morning activity to the final cheer of the day, we make sure every child feels happy, included and genuinely themselves.
Set in the 17-acre grounds of St Francis School, Pewsey, your child has the space to run, explore, try new things and make the kind of friendships that last well beyond the summer.
Why Wiltshire Families Choose St Francis School Summer Day Camp
We believe the best holiday experiences are ones that do more than fill the days. They help children grow. Here is what makes our summer day camp near Marlborough so many families’ first choice:
A Week at Camp: What Your Child Will Experience
Every day at our St Francis School Summer Day Camp is structured to balance energy and imagination — high-energy sport sessions alongside quieter, creative activities that allow every child to shine.
A Typical Day on Camp:
Activities across the week include:
Camp runs Monday to Friday, 8:30am–5:30pm, from 20th July to 21st August 2026. Families can book individual days or full weeks — whatever works best for you.
Football, tennis, basketball and multi-sport sessions
Aeroball, climbing and outdoor adventure activities
Arts, crafts and themed creative projects
Drama, performance games and storytelling
Problem-solving, team-building challenges and brain teasers
Your Child’s Safety and Wellbeing Is at the Heart of Everything We Do
At St Francis, safeguarding and pastoral care are not afterthoughts — they are woven into the fabric of how we work. You can feel confident handing your child over each morning, knowing they are in a setting built on care, professionalism and warmth.
Risk-assessed activity zones, clearly supervised and age-appropriate
What Families Say
“The day camp was the highlight of my son’s summer. He came home excited every single afternoon and couldn’t stop talking about the new friends he’d made.” — Daniel R., Wiltshire
“Fantastic experience from start to finish. The staff were warm, organised, and truly cared about the children. We will absolutely be signing up again.” — Melissa K., Pewsey
“My daughter loved every moment. I felt completely at ease leaving her each day — which says everything.” — Sarah M., Marlboroug
Pricing for Wiltshire Families
We want every family to be able to access our summer holiday programme with confidence. Here is exactly what is included:
Please send your child with a packed lunch and two snacks. Suitable clothing for indoor and outdoor activity is all they need.

Camp Dates 2026
Our St Francis School Summer Day Camp runs across five weeks, with full weekly timetables by age group available to view before you book:
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Week 1: w/c 20th July

Who can attend the St Francis School Summer Day Camp?
Any child from Reception to Year 8 (ages 4–13). You do not need to be a St Francis School pupil — our summer day camp in Wiltshire is open to all children from the local area, including Pewsey, Marlborough, Burbage and beyond.
What should my child bring?
A packed lunch and two snacks, a refillable water bottle, and comfortable clothing suitable for indoor and outdoor activities. On themed days, we will let you know in advance if anything extra is needed.
What are the camp hours?
Camp runs Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:30pm, from 20th July through 21st August 2026.
How do I book a place?
Booking is completed online via our secure portal. Visit the booking page, create or sign in to your account, and select your preferred dates. For any questions, please contact us at daycamps@inspiredlearninggroup.co.uk or call 01672 563228.
Do you accept Tax-Free Childcare?
Yes. We are registered for Tax-Free Childcare and you can apply your government childcare account at checkout.
My child is shy or anxious about joining. Will they be looked after?
Absolutely. Our staff have extensive experience welcoming quieter children and helping them find their feet. Morning welcome activities are designed with this in mind, and every child is placed in a group with peers from their own year to help them settle quickly and comfortably.
For any further information, please email daycamps@inspiredlearninggroup.co.uk

Little Saints
About Little Saints
Little Saints Nursery extended into our purpose built single storey nursery building in September 2017. This allowed us to expand our Nursery provision to welcome babies and toddlers to join our Pre-School children in a setting for children aged 0 to 4 years, open for 51 weeks a year. Our Nursery children have access to 17 acres of glorious school grounds, including a beautiful Forest School in our woodland. Nursery children also have use of the school’s extensive facilities which include a Sports Hall-cum-Theatre, Art & DT Rooms, Cookery Area and two libraries. Healthy meals are cooked in our in-house kitchens and Nursery children in our Pre-School room enjoy eating their lunch in the school Dining Room. Children have weekly French, and PE sessions with specialist teachers. All Nursery children (starting from babies) have music sessions with a specialist music teacher, at least once a week.
At Little Saints Nursery we pride ourselves in creating a home from home environment within which all of our children are loved, cared for and respected as the unique individuals they are. While play and fun are at the heart of all we do, they are underpinned by a fully developed Early Years curriculum, and all activities are carefully designed to help children build the skills they need to start school full of confidence.
All our children, from the youngest babies, follow a specially tailored and richly diverse Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum with access to specialist staff from the Junior School. A wide variety of fun and exciting learning opportunities are provided for the children, which take place both in and out of doors.
We provide a warm, friendly, family atmosphere that encourages a strong link with parents, fostering a bond of trust, where children become confident, happy and independent learners. Each child is treated as an individual from their very first day.
Ofsted report
‘Babies respond positively to the friendly, caring staff and go readily to them for cuddles and reassurance. Staff create a comfortable, welcoming play environment. They are keen to support babies' and toddlers' progress and encourage them to learn through investigation and exploration.’
Little Saints

History
In 1940 Miss Phyllis Burden was approached by a mother to educate her daughter, Miss Burden suggested that the mother needed to find more pupils and on 23 September 1941, St Francis School was founded with just four pupils in the Old Pewsey Rectory. The number of pupils increased and the school moved to much larger premises in Pewsey High Street.
The school flourished and moved to Haybrook House on the current site, in 1984. A charitable trust was formed and in 1990 it acquired the adjacent property, Travancore House. The school now occupies seventeen acres of the glorious Wiltshire countryside in the Pewsey Vale, bordered to the north by the Kennet and Avon canal.
The school has developed and expanded steadily over the years, developing from a small Pre-Preparatory school, into one of Wiltshire’s leading Prep schools, now taking children from 0 – 11. Over the years the school's facilities have been enhanced. The first project was to build a new multi-purpose hall; The Hemery Hall was opened by the Princess Royal in November 1996 and named after the immediate past chairman of governors, David Hemery, who, apart from being an Olympic gold medallist, has had two boys at St Francis. The Hemery Hall has four badminton courts, five-a-side football, tennis, basketball and netball courts, a climbing wall and a sophisticated sound and light system to facilitate the production of school plays and concerts.
The Science laboratory was completed in 1999. This was followed by the addition of a new Junior Nursery for 2 – 3 year olds.
The Phyllis Burden Building was opened in 2004, (and expanded in 2011) giving the Prep Department a Design and Food Technology facility, specialist rooms for French, English, Geography and Religious Studies, as well as three further form rooms.
More recently the Cannon Centre was refurbished and now houses a brand new dedicated DT room, a Drama Studio and modern, state of the art, Science Laboratory. The new purpose built Little Saints Nursery building opened in September 2017 and the Nursery offers care to young children from 0 – 4 years for 51 weeks a year.
St Francis School is a charitable trust, administered by a board of Governors. The School is accredited by the Independent Schools Council.
Phyllis Burden was a great inspiration to us all. She had a great sense of humour and was particularly good at praising success and treating each one of us as an individual. We all loved her and particularly the gold stars she gave to us. She will have been responsible for the nurturing of thousands of young minds and will have contributed greatly to their success in later life.
Tim Devlin, writing on behalf of all six Devlin children who were among her first pupils from 1945-1953. Tim is the ex-national director of I.S.IS., the Independent School’s Information Service

Drama
At St Francis we recognise the importance of Drama and the Performing Arts in our children’s development.
Children from Junior Prep onwards have a weekly Drama lesson which enables them to have a great deal of fun whilst developing their imaginative and presentational skills. Learning how to work together and building up individual self-confidence and ability are of equal importance. Every child is able to take part in at least one exciting performance for parents and friends during the school year and there are other opportunities for acting and reading skills to be displayed at local festivals or within the school community.
LAMDA Tuition
Tuition for LAMDA examinations (The London Academy of Music and Dramatic Arts) is offered as an extra activity with a termly charge for all children in Years 1-6. Lessons are weekly and generally children work in pairs preparing duologues.
LAMDA Information Sheet
Life at St Francis

Music
The Music Department is a flourishing and vibrant department at St Francis School which is led by the Director of Music, Mrs Kay Francis.
75% of pupils from Year 1 to Year 6 are receiving musical tuition on at least one musical instrument. Children are regularly prepared and entered for ABRSM, London College Music and Trinity Rock and Pop examinations. We are proud of the high proportion of pupils who are awarded merit and distinctions for performance on a broad range of instruments.
There are many opportunities for pupils to develop their musical skills outside of their classroom lessons. These ensembles include: Junior Choir (Years 3 & 4) and Senior Choir (Years 5 & 6), Orchestra, Recorder and String groups. In addition, the Music Scholarship Club provides pupils with opportunities to develop their academic understanding of music and their general musicianship. The St Francis String Group consists of pupils from Year 3 upwards and meets every Thursday. The String Group plays in the Carol Service and in other concerts and assemblies during the school year. It has won the Devizes Eisteddfod Ensemble Cup in 2022, 2023 and 2024.
There are plenty of opportunities for pupils to develop into confident and proficient performers.
Termly Music Recitals provide a supportive and friendly platform for pupils to perform solos to family, friends and staff.
The Individual Music Festival, held in the Spring Term provides pupils with a more formal, competitive performance environment. Each year pupils compete in preliminary rounds, for a place in the final competition, adjudicated by guests with specialist knowledge of performance.
The Autumn Term ‘Last Choir Standing’ competition is a celebration of singing across the whole school. Every class from Reception to Year 6, spend Music lessons preparing performances for the school and parents to watch and enjoy. Our external adjudicators award winners to each category and finally the Outstanding choir, known as the ‘Last Choir Standing’.
Past calendar events include collaborations with composer Tom Bayliss and vocal workshops led by the acclaimed Acapella ensemble Apollo 5.

School Admissions
Once you have visited St Francis, we would ask you to register your child(ren) at the earliest possible opportunity, which includes a £75 non-refundable registration fee. Once we have received a registration form, we would then look to arrange a taster day (or session) closer to the time of entry, as well as requesting reports from their current setting.
The taster days and sessions are designed to allow both parties to assess whether St Francis offers an environment in which the child would prosper. Confidential reports from the child’s previous school may be requested. Any specific needs that are identified during the taster day or session will be discussed with the parents. Detailed assessments may take place at the discretion of the Head. Whilst the admissions policy is designed to allow for a broad range of children with differing abilities to take advantage of the educational opportunities on offer at St Francis, the Head retains the right to decline admission to pupils whom they considers to be unable to meet the academic or behavioural standards of the school, and where this could affect the education of other pupils.
Should the taster session go well, and providing a space is available, a formal offer of a place will be made. To accept this place an Acceptance of Place form must be completed and returned along with £500 deposit. All deposits are refundable when a child leaves the School.
Please follow this link to complete our enquiry form for a place for your child in our school.
School Admissions

Community Awards
Community Award assessments are held during the Spring Term each year, they are available for new pupils entering Years 1–5 the following September. Parents are invited to apply for these awards in January, providing that a place is available. These awards are reviewed annually and are dependent on a pupil achieving a consistently high standard of work and progress. Bursaries are available for children throughout the school from the term after free entitlement finishes in Reception through to Year 6. Further details are available from the admissions department admissions@stfpewsey.co.uk
Community Awards
